name: ServiceNow
scope_notes: Release/plugin dependent. API key/HMAC requires com.glide.tokenbased_auth and API-specific policy. Documentation reviewed is Brazil.

controls.name: REST API access policy
controls.what: Per REST API (or globally), lists the inbound authentication profiles allowed, so unlisted credential types such as Basic are refused.
controls.setting: All > System Web Services > REST API Access Policies (map Inbound Authentication Profiles)
controls.quote: Create an API access policy and map an authentication profile to restrict the authentication type for a REST API.

controls.name: API access policy with adaptive authentication filter criteria (IP)
controls.what: An access policy can combine an allowed auth type with filter criteria such as an IP range; other auth types or IPs are denied.
controls.setting: REST API Access Policies + Adaptive Authentication filter criteria
controls.quote: allows only OAuth 2.0 authentication type from a specified range of IP addresses

controls.name: Adaptive authentication policies
controls.what: Allows or denies authentication by IP address, role or group, including for inbound REST API requests.
controls.setting: All > Adaptive Authentication > Authentication Policies / Filter Criteria
controls.quote: You can use the filter criteria of adaptive authentication framework to restrict access to inbound ServiceNow REST APIs.

controls.name: IP Address Access Control
controls.what: Instance-wide allow/deny IP rules for inbound traffic regardless of credential type.
controls.setting: All > System Security > IP Address Access Control (plugin com.snc.ipauthenticator)
controls.quote: Deny: Any IP address in this range cannot interact with this instance unless it is listed in an Allow rule.

controls.name: Enforce Token Restrictions (OAuth application registry)
controls.what: Tokens from this OAuth client work only on APIs whose access policy allows its authentication profile; otherwise they reach any API the user's ACLs allow.
controls.setting: All > System OAuth > Application Registry > [client] > Enforce Token Restrictions
controls.quote: Select to only allow tokens to be used with APIs set to allow the authentication profile.

controls.name: REST API Auth Scope
controls.what: Once an API has an auth scope, only OAuth entities (or API keys) carrying that scope can call it; the useraccount scope bypasses this.
controls.setting: System Web Services > REST API Auth Scope; link scope to OAuth entity / REST API Key
controls.quote: you must associate the same Auth Scope to the OAuth Entity which should have access to this REST API.

controls.name: Access / Refresh Token Lifespan
controls.what: Sets per-client access token (default 1800 s) and refresh token (default 100 days) lifetimes.
controls.setting: All > System OAuth > Application Registry > [client] > Access Token Lifespan / Refresh Token Lifespan
controls.quote: By default, refresh tokens expire in 100 days (8640000 seconds).

controls.name: OAuth application registry Active
controls.what: Deactivating the registry entry stops the OAuth client.
controls.setting: All > System OAuth > Application Registry > [client] > Active
controls.quote: Select the check box to make the application registry active.

controls.name: glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled
controls.what: Inbound OAuth client credentials grant is only available after an admin creates this property and sets it to true.

controls.name: OIDC provider for third-party ID tokens (Active, audience, user claim, JTI)
controls.what: Third-party ID tokens are accepted only via an active OIDC provider record that pins the audience, maps a user claim and can verify JTI.
controls.setting: All > System OAuth > Application Registry > New > Configure an OIDC provider to verify ID tokens (or Machine Identity Console > Inbound integrations)
controls.quote: This value should be the same as the value of the aud claim in the JWT token.

controls.name: Enforce Token Restrictions (OIDC provider)
controls.what: Third-party ID tokens work only on APIs whose access policy enables the ID token authentication profile.
controls.setting: OIDC provider record > Enforce Token Restrictions
controls.quote: Select this option to allow only tokens used with APIs set to enable the authentication profile.

controls.name: REST API Key: Expiry, Active, Auth Scope
controls.what: Each API key can be deactivated, given an expiry (empty means never) and limited by auth scope.
controls.setting: All > System Web Services > API Access Policies > REST API Key
controls.quote: Time after which the credential is no longer valid. Empty value means no expiration.

controls.name: API key / HMAC require a specific API access policy
controls.what: Token-based auth works only on APIs where an access policy lists the API key or HMAC profile; it cannot be added to the global policy.
controls.setting: REST API Access Policies > add API Key / HMAC authentication profile
controls.quote: Token Based Auth isn't allowed in the Global REST API Policy.

controls.name: REST API HMAC secret: Expiry, Active
controls.what: Each HMAC secret can be deactivated and given an expiry (empty means never).
controls.setting: All > System Web Services > API Access Policies > REST API HMAC secret
controls.quote: Time after which the credential is no longer valid. Empty value means no expiration.

controls.name: api_service_admin role (API key / HMAC configuration)
controls.what: Creating API keys and HMAC secrets requires the api_service_admin and adaptive_auth_policy_admin roles; users without them cannot create these credentials.

controls_unknown: Which authentication types the default Global REST API policy allows; the Brazil page names the Global Blocking Policy but does not list them.

anomaly_cues: Spike in oauth_credential rows for one OAuth client
REST transactions by an integration user from a new IP address
Large Table API reads (URL with high sysparm_limit) by OAuth users
Refresh tokens with very long Expires for broad clients

containment.steps: Revoke Access on the token record in Manage Tokens, or call oauth_revoke_token.do with the token; deactivate the OAuth application registry entry; lock the user.
containment.notes: oauth_revoke_token.do or Manage Tokens > Revoke Access marks the given token expired. Docs do not say that revoking a refresh token also expires access tokens already issued from it (default 30-minute life).
